names_aka: gold overlay (US marking synonym for GF-class construction)
leaf gilding: oil gilding, water gilding, verre églomisé (gilded glass), edible-leaf E175
fire gilding: mercury gilding, amalgam gilding, ormolu, wash gilding — HISTORICAL-PROHIBITED, documented for hazard + recognition only
status: active (gold-filled/rolled-gold cladding) | niche (leaf gilding) | historical-prohibited (fire gilding)
principle: Three mechanically-applied gold routes, no electrochemistry. (1) CLADDING/GOLD-FILLED: a slab of solid karat-gold alloy is metallurgically bonded to a base-metal billet (heat + pressure roll/press bonding creates a solid-state diffusion weld), then the composite is rolled to sheet or drawn to wire — the gold layer thins PROPORTIONALLY with the core, so the weight fraction fixed at bonding survives all forming; the surface is genuine wrought karat gold microns-to-tens-of-microns thick, fully ductile because it was never a brittle electro/PVD deposit [FACT: mechanism]. (2) LEAF GILDING: gold beaten to ~0.1 um foil is adhered to a sized (tacky adhesive) or bole-and-glue surface and burnished/sealed — purely adhesive, works on ANY substrate including glass, wood, ceramic [FACT]. (3) FIRE GILDING (mechanism stated for recognition only): gold dissolved in liquid mercury forms a paste amalgam, spread on the metal, then the mercury is driven off as VAPOR by heat, leaving a porous gold layer that is burnished; the vapor step is the reason the process is prohibited — no operating parameters are recorded in this file by policy.

substrates: GF/RGP: brass core is the industry standard (jeweler's brass / commercial-bronze class Cu-Zn ~87-90/10-13) [ESTIMATE: industry typical, high]; sterling and nickel-silver cores exist; STEEL core is NOT standard jewelry GF stock — gold-clad stainless exists as an electronics-contact specialty mill product, not a craft-market item [FACT: trade reality]
leaf: wood, gesso, plaster, glass (verre églomisé via gelatin size), ceramic, metal, paper — conductivity irrelevant
fire gilding (historical): bronze/brass/silver — recognition context for antiques only
applicability.steel_wire_notes: THE STRATEGIC ANSWER TO THE OWNER'S PLATE-THEN-FORM PROBLEM (Q3/Q5): the industry does NOT plate wire then form it — it sells GOLD-FILLED WIRE, clad at the mill, engineered to be coiled, wire-wrapped, bent and drawn AFTER the gold is on, because the skin is ductile wrought karat gold bonded by diffusion weld [FACT: this is the entire gold-filled wire market]. Consequence for the anchor product: keep the ring-forming workflow, SWAP the input from bare steel wire to purchased GF wire (brass core) — every downstream forming question dissolves. What this does NOT give: a steel substrate (spring temper, magnetic sorting, steel price); DIY cladding onto the owner's own steel wire is not feasible (see diy_feasibility). If steel-core is non-negotiable, the plate-first routes in the sibling files with ductile stacks are the only path.
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Leaf gilding is the mechanical route for the houseware extension: glass cups (verre églomisé — gelatin-water size, burnish-look from the glass side), ceramic, wood, frames — zero conductivity requirement, zero bath chemistry. Limits: leaf is ~0.1 um and adhesive-held — decorative surfaces only, not dishwasher-safe, not utensil-wear surfaces; food CONTACT with sized/sealed leaf is a regulatory question [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check per market], though edible 23-24k leaf (E175) applied to food itself is an authorized additive [FACT: E175 exists].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: GF wire gold layer: for 1/20-by-weight 14K on ~1 mm wire, shell thickness computes to roughly 5-10 um — 10-100x the 'gold plated' (0.5 um) and flash (0.05-0.175 um) electroplate classes, and above the 2.5 um 'heavy gold plate'/vermeil thresholds [ESTIMATE: arithmetic from FTC fraction + densities, high]. Marking classes are WEIGHT-FRACTION not thickness: 'gold filled' requires >=10K gold and >=1/20 of total article weight; below 1/20 the fraction must be disclosed as rolled gold plate (e.g. '1/40 12K RGP') [FACT: FTC Guides for the Jewelry Industry, 16 CFR Part 23 class]. Leaf: ~0.08-0.15 um — below flash class, decorative only [FACT: published leaf thickness].

components.name: CLAD-STOCK PRODUCTION LINE (documented so the owner knows why to BUY, not build): bonding furnace/press, breakdown rolling mill, wire draw bench + carbide/diamond dies, inter-pass annealing furnace (controlled atmosphere)
components.purpose: solid-state bond karat-gold slab to core billet, then reduce to gauge over many passes with anneals; the bond forms at high temperature under tonnage-scale pressure with metallurgically clean mating faces
components.diy_notes: NOT a DIY target: tonnage presses, multi-stand rolling, atmosphere anneals, and scrap economics (every failed bond strands karat gold in reject stock) put this at specialist-mill scale; a handful of mills worldwide supply the entire craft trade — the correct 'machine' is a purchase order [FACT: trade structure]

components.name: GF FORMING BENCH (the actual owner machine): ring mandrels (stepped/marked), coil winder or drill-chuck jig, flush cutters, jeweler's saw
components.purpose: wind purchased GF wire into coils, cut into ring blanks (jump-ring method) or size individual rings
components.diy_notes: under-100-USD-class hand tooling; a hand-crank jump-ring winder + saw gives clean parallel cuts; this bench IS the minimum viable jewelry factory for this family

components.name: small jeweler's rolling mill + draw plate (optional)
components.purpose: re-profile GF wire (round -> half-round/square), texture, or size down a gauge
components.diy_notes: GF tolerates rolling/drawing because the clad layer co-deforms; keep reductions moderate and dies polished — a scratched die scores through the gold layer [FACT: co-deformation is the GF design property]

components.name: torch station (small butane/propane-oxy) + solder + flux
components.purpose: close ring joints on GF where cold joins won't do
components.diy_notes: GF soldering is a known skill cliff: overheating diffuses core Cu into the gold skin (permanent dull patch) and melts the thin gold before the core; use easy (low-temp) solder, minimal heat, or design for cold joins (see sequence)

components.name: rotary/vibratory tumbler with steel shot + burnishing soap
components.purpose: work-harden and gloss finished rings; burnishing (not abrasion) is the correct finish for a microns-thick gold skin
components.diy_notes: AVOID aggressive abrasive media/heavy filing/buffing wheels — every um removed is the product; tumble-burnish moves metal instead of removing it

components.name: LEAF KIT: gilder's cushion, gilder's knife, gilder's tip (squirrel-hair transfer brush), agate burnisher, soft mop brushes
components.purpose: cut, lift and lay 0.1 um leaf (untouchable by fingers — it welds to skin moisture) and burnish water-gilt work to mirror
components.diy_notes: complete kits are cheap and standard; 'transfer/patent leaf' (leaf on wax paper backing) removes most of the handling skill for flat-ish houseware

components.name: still air room / draft screen (leaf)
components.purpose: loose leaf is destroyed by any air current

components.name: FIRE GILDING equipment
components.diy_notes: no equipment list is provided by policy; any historical description involving mercury + heat is a non-starter (see safety) [FACT: policy + hazard]

operation_sequence.action: [GF route] source clad stock: buy GF wire/sheet with mill certificate stating construction (e.g. '1/20 14K yellow GF, half-hard, single/double clad')
operation_sequence.parameters: spec: karat (12K/14K typical), fraction (1/20 GF or 1/40 RGP), temper (dead-soft / half-hard / hard), diameter with tolerance
operation_sequence.failure_watch: no certificate = no legal 'gold filled' marking downstream; 'gold filled' claims on plated stock are a known counterfeit problem — verify supplier, spot-assay (see testing)

operation_sequence.action: [GF] verify incoming stock: XRF surface karat, diameter, temper feel; scratch-and-magnet quick screens (GF brass core is non-magnetic — magnetic 'GF' wire is mislabeled)
operation_sequence.parameters: XRF reads karat of skin; fraction needs destructive assay on a sacrificial sample
operation_sequence.failure_watch: surface XRF CANNOT distinguish thick plate from GF — only cross-section or weight assay can; keep retained samples per lot

operation_sequence.action: [GF] wind wire on mandrel (coil for jump-ring-style rings) or bend individual ring blanks
operation_sequence.parameters: mandrel dia = target ID adjusted for springback (half-hard springs back more, holds shape better; dead-soft winds true but dents)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: kinks are permanent (kinked skin work-hardens locally); tool marks from serrated pliers cut the gold skin — use nylon-jaw or smooth pliers

operation_sequence.action: [GF] cut coil into rings with jeweler's saw or shear-action flush cutter
operation_sequence.parameters: saw gives parallel faces for tight closure; cutter is faster but leaves pinch faces
operation_sequence.failure_watch: THE family's one intrinsic defect is born here: cut ends expose the brass core (see defects); plan the closure/finish to hide or seal ends

operation_sequence.action: [GF] close/join: cold-close (twist-shut jump ring), or easy-solder the joint, or design closures that bury ends (wrapped loops, coiled ends)
operation_sequence.parameters: solder: lowest-flow 'easy' gold solder, minimal flame dwell; cold: full twist-close so faces meet under spring tension
operation_sequence.failure_watch: over-torching = Cu diffusion dull spot + possible skin melt; excessive repeated annealing anywhere in the workflow slowly dulls color by core-Cu diffusion into the karat skin [FACT: known GF working limit]

operation_sequence.action: [GF] finish: tumble-burnish with steel shot + burnishing compound; optional light hand-burnish
operation_sequence.parameters: 2-6 h tumble class; burnishing soap per label
operation_sequence.failure_watch: abrasive media / aggressive magnetic pin overuse thins the skin at edges; inspect high-spots after first trials

operation_sequence.action: [GF] QC + mark per testing_acceptance; label with fraction + karat (e.g. 1/20 14K GF) only if supplier cert chain supports it
operation_sequence.parameters: sample-based: appearance, dimensions, closure strength, cut-end exposure check
operation_sequence.failure_watch: marking 'gold filled' without the weight-fraction evidence is a trade-rule violation [FACT: FTC-class marking rules]

operation_sequence.action: [LEAF route, houseware] prepare surface: seal/level (shellac or acrylic ground on wood/ceramic; degrease glass); water gilding instead builds gesso (whiting + hide glue) then bole (clay + glue) layers, each sanded
operation_sequence.parameters: oil gilding: 1-2 seal coats; water gilding: 6-10 gesso + 2-4 bole coats, fully dry
operation_sequence.duration: oil: hours; water: days (the skill- and labor-gate)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: any surface defect telegraphs through 0.1 um leaf perfectly — leaf hides NOTHING

operation_sequence.action: [LEAF] apply size and lay leaf: oil size brushed thin, wait to TACK window, lay leaf with tip; water gilding: flood bole with glue-water, float leaf on
operation_sequence.parameters: oil size tack windows sold as '3-hour' / '12-hour' classes — longer size = higher final gloss [FACT: standard trade practice]
operation_sequence.duration: lay-up minutes per dm2; tack wait per size class
operation_sequence.failure_watch: size too wet = leaf drowns matte/wrinkled; too dry = no adhesion, flakes on skewing; drafts shred loose leaf

operation_sequence.action: [LEAF] skew (brush off overlap flakes — collect skewings, they are gold), fault (patch misses), then burnish (water-gilt only, agate over bole) or leave matte (oil-gilt)
operation_sequence.parameters: burnish after glue firms (same-day window); oil-gilt CANNOT be burnished to mirror [FACT: mechanism — no compliant bole beneath]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: burnishing through the leaf at edges; skewings loss = direct gold loss (~2 g/m2 coverage class [ESTIMATE: arithmetic from leaf thickness, high])

operation_sequence.action: [LEAF] seal if handled/houseware (shellac, lacquer, or 2k clear) — sealing kills some brilliance but is mandatory for touched surfaces
operation_sequence.failure_watch: unsealed oil-gilt handled item sheds gold within weeks; sealed food-CONTACT surfaces remain [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check]

operation_sequence.action: [FIRE GILDING] no operational steps documented — prohibited
operation_sequence.failure_watch: the historical failure mode was the gilder: chronic mercury-vapor poisoning (erethism, 'mad gilder' syndrome) [FACT: occupational-disease history]

composition.hazard_class: elemental Hg: Acute Tox. (inhal.) 2 H330, Repr. 1B H360D, STOT RE 1 H372 (CNS/kidney), Aquatic Chronic 1 H410; vapor exposure during heating is the historically fatal step; mercury use/trade restricted under the Minamata Convention and banned for this purpose in most jurisdictions [FACT]
composition.tag: [FACT: hazard classes; operating parameters withheld by policy]

solutions.maintenance: none — do not operate. Adjacent real-world note: antique fire-gilt (ormolu) objects can retain residual mercury; do not torch, refinish, or ultrasonically strip antique gilt bronze in a home shop [FACT: conservation guidance class]

prep_chain_required: GF forming route: none chemical — clean dry hands/gloves and degreased tools; WHY: the gold surface arrives finished from the mill, every prep step elsewhere in this factory exists to make a deposit stick, and here there is no deposit.
GF torch joints only: flux -> solder -> pickle (solution 1) -> rinse -> neutralize; WHY: strip oxide/flux without abrading the gold skin.

Clad-stock production (industrial, for understanding suppliers): both mating faces milled/brushed to bare clean metal immediately before bonding; WHY: solid-state welds fail on any oxide/organic film — this cleanliness requirement is why cladding is a mill process, not a bench process [FACT: bonding mechanism].

Leaf on houseware: level + seal the substrate (shellac/acrylic), or full gesso+bole for burnished work; degrease glass for verre églomisé; WHY: 0.1 um leaf reproduces every substrate defect and adheres only via the size layer.

deposit_properties.purity_karat: GF: the skin IS a wrought karat alloy — 12K and 14K standard, 10K the legal floor for 'gold filled' marking [FACT: FTC-class rule]; alloy choice sets color (yellow/rose available as stock). Leaf: 22-24K typical (23.75K 'standard gold' leaf), lower-karat and imitation (brass 'Dutch metal') leaves exist — imitation leaf must never be sold as gold [FACT: trade classes].
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: GF skin: karat gold in wrought temper — annealed ~60-100 HV, half-hard/hard-drawn ~130-200 HV class [ESTIMATE: published karat-alloy data, high]; tumble-burnishing work-hardens the surface further. This BEATS soft 24k electroplate for scratch feel without any hardening additives. Leaf: hardness meaningless at 0.1 um — substrate reads through entirely.
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: GF: set at the mill by weight fraction, not per pass — ~5-10 um equivalent shell on 1/20 14K 1 mm wire [ESTIMATE: arithmetic, high], scaling with wire diameter and fraction (1/40 RGP = half). Leaf: 0.08-0.15 um per lay [FACT: published].
deposit_properties.color_control: GF: exact, repeatable, mill-certified — the color is bulk alloy color, immune to bath drift; matching batches years apart is trivial vs plating. Slow color drift only from over-annealing (Cu diffusion) or decades of wear-through. Leaf: karat choice + bole color underneath (red bole = warm, yellow = pale) + burnish vs matte.
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: THE HEADLINE OF THIS FILE: gold-filled stock is the industry's engineered answer to 'form AFTER the gold is on.' The skin is ductile wrought karat gold diffusion-welded to a ductile brass core — the couple co-deforms through winding, bending, moderate drawing and rolling with NO cracking, NO delamination, NO adhesion interface of the electro/PVD kind [FACT: this is the product's design purpose]. Practical limits: (1) CUT ENDS always expose core — design closures that hide/bury them; (2) deep stamping/heavy engraving/aggressive filing cuts through the skin; (3) repeated annealing or over-torching diffuses Cu into the skin and dulls color; (4) springback of half-hard temper must be tooled-for. Heat-forming the owner asked about is largely UNNECESSARY here — GF forms cold. Leaf: not formable at all post-application (crack/shed); gild after forming, always.

testing_acceptance.test: gold weight-fraction assay (destructive, sacrificial sample per lot)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: fire assay / gravimetric strip-and-weigh; the marking claims trace to FTC Guides for the Jewelry Industry (16 CFR Part 23 class)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: gold >= 1/20 of article weight and >= 10K for 'GF' marking; lower fractions marked with true fraction as RGP; supplier mill certificate accepted as primary evidence, spot-verify per new supplier [FACT: rule class]

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class instrumentation, alloy mode
testing_acceptance.acceptance: matches certificate karat; NOTE XRF cannot prove GF-vs-thick-plate construction — pair with cross-section on retained sample

testing_acceptance.test: cross-section layer check (retained sample, new supplier or dispute)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: metallographic mount + microscope; optical layer thickness
testing_acceptance.acceptance: continuous karat layer of computed class thickness, sound bond line, no voids/delamination at interface

testing_acceptance.test: bond integrity / formability of incoming stock
testing_acceptance.standard_class: ASTM B571-class bend: wrap wire around own diameter
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no skin cracking, lifting or flaking at the bend — GF stock PASSES the very test that condemns plated stacks; failure = mill defect, reject lot

testing_acceptance.standard_class: artificial-sweat spot or humidity cabinet class on finished rings
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no green (Cu) corrosion creep from cut ends into wear surfaces within test class; drives closure-design acceptance

testing_acceptance.test: skin-contact metal release (brass core: Cu/Zn; GF is nickel-free by construction unless nickel-silver core)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: EN 1811 applies to nickel only — confirm core alloy is Ni-free; Cu/Zn release unregulated for jewelry class [FACT: regulation scope]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: core alloy certificate Ni-free; if nickel-silver core ever used, EN 1811 send-out required

testing_acceptance.standard_class: tape-pull + soft-cloth rub cycles (workshop class, no formal standard)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no lift on tape, no gold transfer to cloth after sealing; faults patched before seal

testing_acceptance.standard_class: FTC 16 CFR Part 23 class terms: 'gold filled', 'rolled gold plate', 'gold leaf/gilded', never 'solid gold'
testing_acceptance.acceptance: labels match construction evidence; imitation leaf never sold as gold [FACT: rule class]

defects_and_remedies.defect: green/dark corrosion or skin discoloration at ring cut ends
defects_and_remedies.cause: exposed brass core at every cut — intrinsic to clad construction
defects_and_remedies.remedy: design-level: wrapped/coiled closures that bury ends, solder-close and dress the joint, or accept-and-declare; NOT fixable by 'more gold' — it is geometry

defects_and_remedies.cause: Cu diffused from core into karat skin under excess heat
defects_and_remedies.remedy: lowest-temp solder, minimal dwell, heat-sink the work; patch is permanent — prevention only

defects_and_remedies.defect: skin cracks or lifts during forming (rare on genuine GF)
defects_and_remedies.cause: counterfeit stock (plated sold as GF), mill bond defect, or gross over-work (repeated reverse bends at one point)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: bend-test incoming lots; single-direction forming; reject/report bad lots — genuine GF surviving the wrap test will survive ring forming

defects_and_remedies.defect: wear-through to core at high spots after years of wear
defects_and_remedies.cause: microns-thick skin has a finite (but long) wear budget; abrasive finishing accelerated it
defects_and_remedies.remedy: burnish-don't-abrade finishing discipline; choose 1/20 over 1/40 stock for daily-wear items; honest lifetime claims (years-decades vs months for plate) [FACT: relative wear class]

defects_and_remedies.defect: tool marks / scored gold from pliers and dies
defects_and_remedies.cause: serrated jaws, scratched draw dies, gritty mandrel
defects_and_remedies.remedy: nylon-jaw/smooth polished tooling only; inspect and polish dies; the skin cannot be re-plated over damage — surface discipline is the yield lever

defects_and_remedies.defect: steel tweezers turned pink / everything copper-flashed in pickle
defects_and_remedies.cause: iron in Cu-loaded pickle sets up immersion copper deposition
defects_and_remedies.remedy: copper/plastic tongs only in pickle; replace saturated pickle [FACT: classic bench error]

defects_and_remedies.cause: size laid too wet (drowned) or past tack (no bond); drafts during lay
defects_and_remedies.remedy: tack-test on scrap, work the size window, screen drafts; refloat/patch faults before sealing

defects_and_remedies.defect: burnished water-gilt crazes or sheds in humid use
defects_and_remedies.cause: hide-glue/gesso ground is water-sensitive for life
defects_and_remedies.remedy: water gilding only for dry-display items; use oil gilding + seal for handled houseware

defects_and_remedies.cause: imitation (brass) leaf used, or genuine leaf worn through unsealed
defects_and_remedies.remedy: buy certified gold leaf, seal handled surfaces, never market imitation as gold [FACT: trade-rule class]

cost_drivers: GF stock premium: the wire price carries real gold at 1/20 weight — material cost per ring is dominated by gold content, but with ZERO bath, rectifier, waste-stream or chemistry-babysitting overhead: near-pure material + labor economics
scrap is an ASSET not waste: GF offcuts/ends are 5% gold by weight — collect and sell to refiner; leaf skewings likewise; this family's 'waste stream' has positive value
no gold inventory tied up in baths (vs 1-8 g Au locked in every plating tank in the sibling files)
tooling capex tiny (mandrels, cutters, tumbler); clad-stock production capex is astronomical and permanently outsourced to the mill — the buy-vs-build answer is structural
labor per piece is the main cost: winding/cutting/closing/finishing is hand time; jump-ring-style batching amortizes it
leaf: gold cost ~2 g/m2 [ESTIMATE: arithmetic, high] is trivial per piece — labor and ground preparation (especially water gilding, days) dominate utterly
certification/assay: per-lot verification cost of GF claims (XRF quick, occasional destructive assay), cheaper than the recurring bath-analysis of every wet route
market note: GF commands the 'demi-fine' price band above plated and below karat — the construction IS the marketing claim, protect it with the cert chain

hazards: FIRE GILDING (the reason this family carries a prohibited tier): elemental mercury — Acute Tox. inhalation 2 (H330), Repr. 1B (H360D), STOT RE 1 CNS/kidney (H372), Aquatic Chronic 1 (H410); the process step IS mercury-vapor generation by heating; historical gilder cohorts suffered chronic mercurialism (erethism); mercury supply/use restricted under the Minamata Convention; prohibited for any owner activity [FACT]
antique fire-gilt objects can retain residual mercury — refinishing/torching antique ormolu releases Hg vapor [FACT: conservation-class warning]
pickle acids (NaHSO4/H2SO4): corrosive/irritant; Cu-laden spent pickle aquatic-toxic [FACT]
mechanical: wire whip from coiled stock, flying cut ends (eye), saw/cutter lacerations, rolling-mill pinch [FACT: class]
gesso/whiting sanding dust: nuisance dust class [FACT]
leaf and GF working involve NO cyanide, NO nickel (with brass-core stock), NO hot process baths — the lowest chemical-hazard family in this factory [FACT: by construction]
controls: absolute prohibition on fire gilding: no mercury on site, ever; decline antique-regilding work
eye protection for cutting/winding; guard the mill nip; cut inside a box or with hold-down to catch flying ends
pickle: goggles/gloves, bicarbonate neutralization, Cu-waste to collection not drain; copper tongs only
flammable size and shellac: no open flame in the gilding corner; solvent rags in lidded metal bin
trade-honesty control: certificate chain for every GF lot and every leaf book (imitation leaf segregated and labeled) — mislabeling is the family's main 'incident' class
safety.waste: Smallest waste footprint in the factory: (1) GF offcuts + leaf skewings -> refiner (revenue, not disposal); (2) spent Cu-laden pickle, neutralized -> metal-bearing-waste collection; (3) solvent rags/size residues -> flammables disposal; (4) NO gold-bath, cyanide, nickel or mercury streams exist so long as the fire-gilding prohibition holds. Local rules for (2)-(3) [UNKNOWN — needs local regulation check].

diy_feasibility.verdict: HIGHEST-FEASIBILITY ROUTE IN THE ENTIRE FACTORY for the anchor product, with one structural swap: do not CLAD, do not PLATE — BUY gold-filled wire and run a forming-and-finishing micro-factory. This dissolves the owner's hardest question (plate-then-form on wire) because the mill already solved it metallurgically; it also removes every bath, rectifier, vacuum chamber and hazardous-chemistry dependency, at the price of (a) brass core instead of steel and (b) paying for real gold content per meter. Leaf gilding: fully DIY-feasible for the houseware/decor extension (glass, wood, frames) — decorative, sealed, honestly-marketed surfaces only. Clad-stock PRODUCTION at home: NO — mill-scale bonding/rolling/drawing. Fire gilding: PROHIBITED, no conditions.

No rectifier, no vacuum, no gold bath. [ESTIMATE: setup class, high confidence on list, no invented prices]
